prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Draw a clean mechanical detail sheet of the EXACT COMPACT FOREARM ARMOR AND GIANT FIST ON REFERENCE 1, showing its resting and opened states. Reference 1's installed fist/arm size and silhouette are the PRIMARY AUTHORITY. Reference 2 clarifies the installed short outer shell and bent arm. Reference 3 only explains the shell-opening principle. Reference 4 supplies train window/stripe/cab identity.

CRITICAL: design the heavy humanoid forearm FIRST, then its compact train-derived outer armor. DO NOT DRAW A LONG WHOLE TRAIN CAR WITH A FIST STUCK TO ITS END. DO NOT SCALE THE FIST DOWN. The huge fist must occupy roughly 35-40% of elbow-to-knuckle projected length, as in the approved robot. The arm housing is only about 1.3 times the fist's longitudinal length, NOT three/four fist lengths. No fully sealed sleeve. This is an external shell on the outside of the original arm; its inner and lower side remains visibly open to expose the thick orange/graphite original forearm and wrist. No passenger seats or full railway doors.

Layout: TWO large panels SIDE BY SIDE, warm ivory background, SAME three-quarter viewing angle and SAME bent-arm pose in both. Short white/orange upper-arm stump at upper left, bent elbow behind at top, forearm slopes DOWN-RIGHT and the heavy clenched giant fist points DOWN-RIGHT. The rounded blue-glazed train CAB NOSE sits behind the forearm near the ELBOW / upper left. It never points toward the knuckles. The split former central coupling end is toward the wrist/lower right. Show complete fist, thumb and elbow, no head/torso/legs. The outer train shell's blue cab glass, TWO large blue side-window zones, orange stripe, ivory armor shape and graphite lower lip look like references 1 and 2, not a full long passenger carriage.
LEFT: REST / folded-close outer protective cradle. Keep the inner-side underside long opening visible, with the thick reinforced arm beneath. The wrist and whole giant knuckles extend beyond the shell front. A small original train side fin is folded FLUSH into its shell edge.
RIGHT: SAME arm and SAME fist stay absolutely unmoved, the same TWO longitudinal shell halves swing sideways away from that arm on hinge rails, one toward the viewer and the other away. They reveal the same orange/graphite arm frame. Their front half-rims describe the open cannon channel around the forearm BEHIND the giant fist, not a long separate barrel or a second gun. The rear cab nose remains an intact short cab cap near the elbow; only the middle longitudinal panels open. Small train fin stays folded flush against its own half-shell, not a large wing. One restrained orange curved arrow per half-shell shows motion.
Exactly same elbow/wrist/knuckle locations, giant fist proportions, shell lengths, window locations and orange stripe between panels. Show one thin cyan wrist seam at the same original wrist position, partly occluded by wrist armor. No extra blue lights.

Match approved clean inked orange/ivory/graphite kinetic cel art and faceted material shading. Detailed but not covered in random greebles. No words, letters, logos or decorative diagram frames. Generous outer margin; do not crop.
